title: Agentic Evaluations at Scale, For Everybody — Nicholas Kang & Michael Aaron, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: Kaggle/DeepMind presenters describe their eval platforms (hackathons, agent exams, Game Arena, community benchmarks) and the problems that motivated them: scattered/stale evals, opaque harnesses, and saturation. The most transferable content is their observation that agent performance is dominated by the harness, not the model, and their use of pairwise Bradley-Terry scheduling to cut the number of expensive runs needed for statistical significance.

takeaways.what_they_do: They separate what is being tested (model vs harness) and cite evidence that the scaffold dominates coding scores, so a benchmark result without a fixed harness is not comparable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The thing that really matters a lot for coding performance is what harness is it running inside of with like a 22% difference depending on the harness.
takeaways.numbers: ~22% performance difference attributable to harness; six frontier models within a couple of percentage points on SWE-bench Pro

takeaways.technique: Pairwise Bradley-Terry scheduling to cut runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of running every model against every other many times, they schedule a sparse set of pairwise matchups using Bradley-Terry to reach statistical significance with far fewer games.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It uses Bradley-Terry pairwise to try to like not have too many games we have to run.
takeaways.numbers: ~400,000 poker hands needed for significance without it

takeaways.what_they_do: Each eval task combines deterministic assertions (contains X, produced valid output) with LLM judging, grouped into tasks and aggregated into a benchmark, with side-by-side comparison.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you write some assertions... We also do LLM judging similar to the production platforms. Uh these all get grouped together in a task.

takeaways.technique: Cheap baseline exam before real-world deployment
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue agents are shipped without any pre-deployment test and propose a quick standardized exam as a baseline gate before an agent runs in the real world.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most of them aren't actually testing their agents before they're sending them out to the real world.

takeaways.technique: Model proxy for consistent multi-model access
takeaways.what_they_do: All game/eval runs talk to models through a single LLM model proxy so every model is called the same way and comparisons are fair.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We use LLM model proxy... to just like talk in a consistent way to all of the models that we want to run these games against.

takeaways.what_they_do: A lab re-ran a benchmark using its own API compaction and got much better numbers, showing that unequal per-model configuration invalidates cross-model comparisons.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they were optimizing it for their model. So, they had used compaction that they had provided through their API, and we didn't for all of the models we ran.
